articleTitle: Attention in Focus: Transformer-Powered Super-Resolution for Advanced Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated outstanding performance in natural language processing and computer vision tasks due to their ability to manage long-range dependencies. However, when applied to super-resolution of remote sensing images, transformer-based methods often produce overly smooth results that lack necessary textural details. To overcome this challenge, we developed the Multi-Attention Residual Transformer (MART). MART utilizes a Multi-Scale Attention Module to integrate information at different scales, effectively restoring the complex details in remote sensing images. With its hybrid attention mechanism, MART captures both local and global features efficiently. Comprehensive evaluations on various remote sensing datasets reveal that MART significantly enhances image quality. Compared to widely used advanced methods, MART excels in both qualitative and quantitative metrics, effectively restoring a wide range of landmark features.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Path Planning for Coastal Area Maritime Wireless Communication Networking Based on Policy Gradient and Squirrel Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the trend of developing “low altitude economy” nowadays, the solution of using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm as a complementation to fixed wireless communication base stations (BSs) along the coastline to meet the requirements of communication for maritime activities in coastal area, is promising and has attracted a lot attention. In the process of wireless communication networking, it is important for UAVs to use their flexibility advantage of being movable, approaching the areas with the highest wireless communication demand and providing necessary coverage, thus, it is highly worthy of study the path planning issue of UAVs in UAV swarms used for maritime wireless communication. Till now, although some studies have been conducted on multi-UAV path planning at sea, most of them are not aimed at ensuring wireless communication in coastal area. In this paper, a multi-UAV path planning method for coastal area maritime wireless communication based on policy gradient and squirrel search algorithm has been proposed, which can provide more efficient path planning support for individuals in UAV swarm. Via numerical experiment, the effectiveness of proposed method has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on High-Precision Calculation Methods for Stellar Apparent Positions for A Satellite Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Based on the needs for sub-arcsecond attitude determination of microsatellites, a high-precision attitude determination method can be employed without additional payloads by reusing onboard scientific cameras. This method utilizes the peripheral high-quality imaging areas of its square-shaped detector, achieving a closed-loop high-precision attitude determination decoupled from the working of the scientific camera. The high-precision stellar apparent position calculation for a satellite observer is fundamental for achieving high-precision astronomical attitude determination. Due to the optical sensors being on a satellite moving at high speeds in orbit, the aberration caused by satellite motion cannot be ignored. Moreover, other methods for calculating stellar apparent positions based on motion platforms often require improved calculation accuracy. Therefore, this paper conducts research on high-precision calculation methods for stellar apparent positions for a satellite observer. It constructs a high-precision navigational star catalog using the highest precision 3D data of the Milky Way, Gaia EDR3, to correct for the aberration caused by satellite motion, achieving accuracy superior to other motion platform-based methods. The precision reaches the milliarcsecond level, meeting the requirements for sub-arcsecond or even higher precision astronomical attitude determination for satellites.

articleTitle: Pulse Signal Recognition Based on EfficientNetV2_ResBlock Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In the process of pulse signal recognition analysis, methods in the time domain, frequency domain, and time-frequency domain are difficult to deeply extract the nonlinear features of pulse signals. Moreover, traditional machine learning requires manual feature definition and cannot perform self-learning of features. Therefore, this paper proposes a pulse signal recognition analysis method based on the EfficientNetV2_ResBlock network. Compared with previous methods that use features for pulse recognition, this paper uses two-dimensional images for pulse recognition, fully retaining the feature information of the pulse signals and improving recognition accuracy. Using GAF (Gramian Angular Field), the one-dimensional pulse time series is converted into two-dimensional images. The Efficient-NetV2_ResBlock network model is used to analyze and recognize pulse signals and to establish a pulse signal classification model. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves an average recognition accuracy of 97.9% for pulse recognition, with the recognition accuracy for abrupt pulse and floating pulse reaching 100%. Compared with other convolutional neural networks, the proposed model has higher accuracy, shorter training time, and fewer network parameters.

articleTitle: Delay Distribution-Based Smith Predictor for Networked Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this work, we study the discrete-time networked control systems (NCSs) with network-induced dual channel delays. In a sampling period, if the feedback-channel delay is historical information for the controller node, then the forward-channel delay is an unknown future quantity. The typical Smith predictor scheme usually treats the forward-channel delay as a measurable historical quantity, which makes it not reasonably compensated. In this paper, a novel Smith predictor scheme is proposed to compensate for dual-channel delays and assist in controller design, which utilizes information about the distribution of forward-channel delays to predictively compensate for them. Then, the methods for determining the stability condition of the system and the controller feedback gain that account for delay distribution are provided. Finally, two simulation examples are given to show that the proposed scheme achieves better state convergence and tracking performance under varying network conditions compared to typical Smith predictor schemes.

articleTitle: Barrier Construction of the Homicidal Chauffeur Game Considering Speed Descent of the Car
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The Homicidal Chauffeur game is a classic pursuit-evasion problem for its significant application in aerospace, robot control, and military. Different from the well-known Isaacs' Homicidal Chauffeur game in which the car's speed is constant, we assume that the car's speed decreases during turns, reflecting the energy limitations in real-world applications. The paper aims to derive the optimal strategies and construct a barrier separating the capture and evasion zones. Initially, we simplify the six- dimensional problem to a three-dimensional one. Subsequently, we deduce the optimal strategy and construct the barrier using the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation and backward induction method. A new barrier appears where the optimal strategy of the pursuer is different from the traditional one. That is, when the pursuer's speed is greater than a critical value, the optimal strategy is to apply maximum control; when the pursuer's speed is less than the critical speed, the optimal strategy is to apply zero control.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Adaptive Actuator Failure Compensation Control for Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive tracking control scheme for nonlinear satellite systems with dynamic uncertainty and unknown actuator failures. A fixed-time adaptive fault-tolerant control scheme is designed by incorporating an adaptive actuator failure compensation method into a smooth function-based backstepping control framework. The control scheme can ensure that its signals remain bounded in the presence of dynamic uncertainties and unknown actuator failures in the satellite system. Additionally, it ensures that the tracking error converges to a predetermined interval within a fixed time. Finally, we demonstrated the effectiveness of the program by performing simulation experiments based on a geostationary orbit satellite.

articleTitle: Research on Vector Control Simulation of Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Vector control is an important control method of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). On the basis of analyzing the mathematical model and vector control principle of PMSM, the vector control simulation model of PMSM was established by Matlab/Simulink software. Through simulation analysis, the influence characteristics and change rules of the dynamic change of speed and torque were discussed, and the validity of the simulation model and the correctness of the control algorithm were verified, which provides a theoretical basis for the design and debugging of the control system of PMSM.

articleTitle: A Novel Edge Computing Deployment Scheme Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles and Buses for Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Deploying edge servers on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has become a promising strategy to handle the spatiotemporally varying user demands on ground. However, a critical limitation of the UAVs is the limited flight endurance caused by the limited power supply. To this end, we propose in this paper a novel edge computing deployment scheme using UAVs and buses for Internet of Vehicles. The UAV-mounted edge servers (UAVESs) act as quick-response mobile servers to serve the workload hotspots, while buses offer energy-efficient transportation and charging service for these UAVs. Firstly, we use Temporal Mean Shift Clustering (TMSC) to identify the workload hotspots on the map of an IoV system at different time slots. Next, we design a Bus-Assisted UAV Scheduling (BA-UAVS) strategy to serve the user demand on the map. BA-UAVS selects a minimum number of bus routes to cover the maximum number of hotspots, and then schedules the UAVs along with the operation of the selected buses to reduce the fly distance, i.e., the cost. Finally, we conduct extensive trace-driven simulations on a real dataset, and the experimental results verify that our approach improves the service utilization and reduces the cost significantly compared with the approaches with no bus assistance.

articleTitle: Implementation of Automaton Product Networks: From Formal Language to Algebraic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper investigates the construction of automaton product networks based on the algebraic model of automata. By defining the vector forms of states and events in automaton product networks, we establish algebraic models for these networks. Based on this algebraic model, we derive the state transition function in vector form for automaton product networks. Utilizing the equivalence relationship between the established state transition function and the dynamic structure matrix, we design synthesis formulas for automaton product networks in two scenarios: the shared event set scenario and the general scenario. The synthesis formulas we designed can handle complex network operations, improving computational efficiency and accuracy, while also avoiding the common storage complexity explosion problem found in algebraic methods.

articleTitle: Research on Ascent Phase Guidance Technology Based on Uncertainty Parameter Online Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In response to the challenges of numerous constraints in the ascent phase of composite-powered carriers, narrow flight corridors, and poor adaptability of guidance to deviations in aerodynamic coefficients, atmospheric density, and thrust, this paper proposes an ascent guidance method based on online identification of uncertain parameters. An online identification model based on acceleration information is established to identify the magnitude of parameter deviations. Trajectory profiles matching the magnitude of parameter deviations are selected online from a trajectory database to ensure that the guided vehicle reaches the starting window of the next mission within the constraints under deviation conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that this method enables rapid online selection of a trajectory adapted to the current composite uncertainties, thereby enhancing the robustness of ascent phase guidance schemes for composite-powered carriers.

articleTitle: An Improved Imitation Learning Algorithm Based on Markov Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: An improved imitation learning algorithm based on Markov chain is proposed, aiming to enhance the performance of autonomous driving in complex environments. Imitation learning learns task execution by observing expert behavior, while Markov chains are used to model state transition processes. The existing imitation learning algorithms have limited ability to handle complex tasks, especially in natural environments. The algorithm proposed in this article improves learning efficiency and autonomous control performance by introducing strategy iteration and reward function design for sudden obstacles. The core idea is to introduce Markov decision processes into traditional imitation learning frameworks to improve learning efficiency and performance. By acquiring a refined strategy, the objective is to mimic the agent's actions within the environment to closely resemble those of the expert. To achieve this, first train an initial strategy using expert examples. Then, use this strategy to generate new examples and update the strategy using these examples. This process iterates continuously until the strategy converges. The experimental results show that on the lunar environment autonomous driving datasets, the accuracy of our algorithm reaches 95% with a mean square error of 0.02, while the accuracy of the comparative algorithm is the highest at 90% with a mean square error of 0.05. This indicates that the improved algorithm can more accurately learn and imitate the driving behavior of experts. In addition, the performance of the algorithm is stable at different iteration times, indicating good convergence.

articleTitle: Beam Direction Estimation for Spaceborne Circular Scanning Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Due to the rotation of spaceborne circular scanning radar antenna, the beam direction is varying in nearly conical shape, which complicates the beam direction calibration than the fixed antenna. In this paper, a beam direction estimation method for circular scanning radar based on echo parameter is demonstrated, which do not depend on calibrator, and facilitates the calibration test.

articleTitle: Design of JPEG2000 Image Compression System Based on ADV212 for Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Due to the limitations of spacecraft data processing capabilities and the data transmission rate to the ground, the image compression system is essential for imaging payloads on satellites. JPEG2000, with its advantages of high compression ratio, high signal-to-noise ratio, support for progressive transmission, and absence of mosaic distortion, is a preferred algorithm for image compression in spaceborne cameras. In response to the complexity of the JPEG2000 algorithm and the challenges of hardware implementation, this paper presents an image compression system based on the ADV212 image compression chip for realizing JPEG2000 compression. The FPGA is utilized for image buffering and control of the compression system, while the ADV212 chip performs the compression functions. The experimental results validate the high performance and compatibility of the system. This system boasts advantages such as simple hardware and software implementation, high efficiency, superior performance, short development cycle, and low cost, which makes it suitable for aerospace applications, particularly in commercial space satellites.

articleTitle: Scenario-Based Aircraft Nose Wheel Steering Control Modes Design and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The Nose Wheel Steering System is a sub-system of the Landing Gear System, which provides on-ground operations not only to the aircraft and the pilots but also to the ground crews. In this paper, the steering control modes are designed through a scenario-based approach, and three control modes are determined. The conditions for transitions between control modes are studied in detail. A model is built in MATLAB Stateflow based on the control modes and simulations conducted for three main scenarios verify the design. Limitations of the model such as assumptions of the scenarios are also included.

articleTitle: A Time-Varying Sea Clutter Simulation Method in Bistatic SARa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Spaceborne bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has the advantages of multi-angle coverage, high-resolution imaging, and all-weather, all-day operational capability, making it highly valuable for sea surface target detection. However, sea clutter is a major source of interference in this process, affecting the accuracy of target detection. Due to the complex propagation paths and signal processing involved in bistatic SAR, the modeling of sea clutter remains a significant challenge. Currently, sea clutter modeling for bistatic SAR primarily employs geometric optics, physical optics, or hybrid methods, but these approaches are computationally intensive. This paper proposes a time-varying sea surface echo simulation method for bistatic SAR, which accurately calculates the backscattering coefficient of the sea surface and incorporates dynamic simulation of rough sea surfaces. The method provides high-precision simulations of sea surface scattering characteristics. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Temperature Stability for the Filament Current Controller in Spaceborne Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The regulation range and ripple of the filament current in a time-of-flight mass spectrometer directly impact the electron emission capability and stability, which are crucial performance indicators for determining ionization efficiency. This paper systematically investigates the temperature stability of the filament drive circuit in a mass spectrometer and designs a constant current drive circuit based on the RSS0508HRH chip. Through simulation analysis, methods for optimizing circuit stability are proposed and validated through experiments. The research results demonstrate that the constant current drive circuit designed with the RSS0508HRH chip achieves closed-loop feedback regulation of the filament emission current. The experiment conducted over a wide temperature range of −40°C to 75°C, the current remained stable, with an error margin controlled within 3%. The experimental data further confirm that this constant current drive circuit exhibits excellent temperature adaptability and stability, meeting the application requirements of mass spectrometers across varying temperature environments.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Real-Time Distributed Simulation System Architecture Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: High-precision real-time distributed simulation scheduling has been a research hotspot in recent years. The requirements for distributed simulation scheduling mechanisms in real-time distributed simulation scheduling services largely determine the accuracy and real-time performance of the simulation system. To address the issue that traditional simulation methods struggle to ensure synchronization and consistency between simulation timing and control timing in safety-critical fields such as aerospace, which may lead to significant potential risks in subsequent testing and usage, this paper designs a high-precision real-time distributed simulation system architecture. It focuses on three core technical aspects of the architecture: real-time performance, high precision, and distribution. Through testing and analysis, it is concluded that the high-precision real-time distributed simulation system architecture designed in this paper improves the real-time performance and accuracy of simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Aviation Equipment Support Capability Based on Factor Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Aviation equipment maintenance support indexes are not only important parameters for PHM (prognostic and health management) analysis, but also important parameters to measure the support ability of aviation equipment. Aviation equipment support capability involves a large number of indexes (variables), which is a difficult problem for its monitoring and evaluation. This paper presents an evaluation method of aviation equipment support capability based on factor analysis model. This method extracts the independent influence factors through the dimension reduction method of factor analysis, and effectively reduces the difficulty of analyzing the influence factors of aviation equipment support capability evaluation under the premise of retaining most of the information of the original data. Thus, the information overlap between samples is eliminated and the problem is simplified. The example shows that the method can effectively reduce the dimension of variables and the workload in the evaluation process.

articleTitle: Reliability Design Methods for Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a reliability design methodology for autonomous systems, building a reliability requirement framework through model-based requirements analysis and functional design. The paper starts from the characteristics of perception, decision-making, action, and monitoring in autonomous systems, and decomposes the functional, performance, resource, environmental, and quantitative reliability requirements. It defines the system's functional architecture and conducts failure analysis, uncovering shortcomings in the initial design. In response to failure scenarios such as functional loss, degradation, and mismatch, this paper proposes improvement strategies, including redundancy design, margin design, and multi-version algorithms, aiming to enhance task success rates and reliability. Ultimately, the paper provides a comprehensive reliability design framework and practical guidance for the safe operation of autonomous systems in complex environments.

articleTitle: Energy-Consumption Optimization Control for Lunar Rover's Travel with Torque-Distribution-strategy in Rear Wheels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In anticipation of future extensive lunar surface operations, lunar rovers are required to advance towards higher speeds and improved energy conservation. When traveling at high speeds on the lunar surface, the vehicle's energy expenditure is greatly amplified by the influence of the terrain, particularly in conditions where driving and steering are coupled. This paper proposes an energy-saving control strategy for lunar rovers that employs dynamic rear-axle torque distribution, with the goal of optimizing transient energy consumption during travel. To tackle the challenge of non-differentiable functions within the optimization objectives, we suggest using a zeroth-order gradient optimization method for resolution, dynamically constraining the range of control parameters to fulfill the dynamic torque distribution objectives as needed for the task. The energy-saving control effectiveness of the algorithm has been confirmed through simulation, demonstrating a minimum energy-saving ratio of at least 4%, which increases to over 11% as the speed level rises, offering a valuable technical solution for the energy optimization of lunar rovers.

articleTitle: Data Modeling and Simulation Method of Full-Link Spaceborne Microwave Scatterometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In order to support the design demonstration of the space-based observation system of the global ocean wind field and the optimization design of the ocean satellite, a full-link spaceborne microwave scatterometer modeling method is proposed. According to the set simulated wind field, and the satellite orbit and scatterometer observation mechanism, a wind field calculation model for the scatterometer beam observation position at each moment is established. Based on the principle of radar observation and Geophysics model function, the calculation model of echo power and backscatter coefficient is constructed by superposing the instruments observation noise and Geophysics noise. The space grid of the earth's surface is divided, and the backscatter coefficient is registered into each space grid by using the distance weighted average method. The SNR and radiometric accuracy of each grid are obtained. Finally, the maximum likelihood method is used to retrieve the wind field from the simulated data. The simulation results show that the principle of the modeling method is correct, and the simulation accuracy of the model with wind speed better than 2m / s and wind direction better than 20 ° can be obtained, which meets the needs of engineering design demonstration.

articleTitle: A Reliability Test Scenario Generation Method for Unmanned Vehicle Off-Road Tracking Task Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: It is important to conduct simulation tests of unmanned vehicles (UV). However, some test scenario generation methods face challenges such as a lack of off-road scenarios and insufficient consideration of interferences. This paper proposes an unmanned vehicle off-road task reliability test scenario generation method. First, the static test environment is built based on the TORCS simulation platform. Subsequently, different types of unmanned vehicle-target vehicle (TV) tracking interaction behaviour models are generated based on the modified DDPG method. Finally, the unmanned vehicle task reliability test under different disturbances is achieved. The results show that the method can not only effectively generate off-road tracking test scenarios, but also adjust the interference to test unmanned vehicles' task reliability. The method provides valuable guidance for testing and enhancing the reliability of the model to some degree.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Extraction Methods for Key Regions in Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In response to the problem of high complexity and inaccurate extraction of key areas in hyperspectral satellite images, this paper proposes an intelligent extraction method for key areas in hyperspectral images. Firstly, the feature layer fusion target spectral signal matching detection method is adopted, and the subspace projection method is used to suppress background clutter signals and enhance the contrast between the target and background clutter to extract the target area. In the absence of any prior information on key area targets, this method uses anomaly detection algorithms to perform coarse screening on abnormal areas. Finally, key area detection is achieved through the fusion of target spectral signal matching detection and anomaly detection decision level fusion in the feature layer. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively suppress clutter signals, enhance the distinguishability between targets and backgrounds, and handle situations whether or not the prior spectral information is known. Moreover, the algorithm has strong robustness and low processing complexity.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Shared Control Method and Automatic Assistance for Aircraft Under Pilot-Induced Oscillations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper presents a new human-machine shared control method to improve the control performance of the aircraft in abnormal situations. To solve the problem of Pilot-Induced Oscillations(PIO) caused by elevator rate limitation, a shared control method based on autopilot assistance is designed by adjusting the gain of the pilot's control command. This method takes advantage of the precision control of the autopilot and corrects the pilot's excessive control behavior, thereby enhancing the stability of the aircraft in complex environments. The key feature of the proposed shared control is that it utilizes the control command of the autopilot to achieve the process of assisting the pilot in flying, which helps reduce the pilot's high control gain while keeping the elevator away from saturation. At the same time, considering the fact that the pilot's instantaneous judgment of triggering a fault has certain ambiguity, the pilot's adaptive logic trigger module is utilized with fuzzy logic. Finally, the effectiveness of the shared controller is verified by the experimental simulation of F-16 longitudinal dynamics under abnormal conditions.

articleTitle: Parallel Simulation of Acoustic Characteristics for Near-Surface Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a parallel acoustic characterization simulation method for near-surface targets. This method is based on the Shooting and Bouncing Ray (SBR)) method and allows for the high-precision simulation of near-surface target acoustic characteristics. Furthermore, it enables the acceleration of the simulation computation process of complex shape near-surface targets by utilizing a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) platform. By employing an equivalent decomposition of near-surface target acoustic field echoes, the task scale of 10 billion acoustic beam lines is exceeded on a multi-GPU cluster, thereby enabling the rapid and precise simulation of the acoustic characteristics of large near-surface targets. This approach has significant potential for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Structural Simplification of Finite State Machines using Pruning Operators based on Semi-Tensor Product of Matrices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of structural simplification of finite state machines (FSMs), aiming at designing a structural simplification filter for FSMs by constructing pruning operators within the framework of the semi-tensor product of matrices (STP), where the FSM is considered as a logical dynamical system. The concept of pruning operators is proposed by incorporating the physical meaning of FSM state transitions into its dynamic equations. Therefore, to simplify the FSM state space, we construct pruning operators for eliminating redundant states and their additional transitions, respectively. In addition, we further design the corresponding algorithms based on these mathematical descriptions to make the physical meaning of FSM state-space optimization clearer. The validity and correctness of the conclusions are verified using the corresponding language models. The proposed pruning operators lay the foundation for performing state-space optimization and may have a wide range of application scenarios.

articleTitle: Lunar Rover's Path Tracking Control Strategy Using Zero-Order Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The development of lunar rovers is critical for human exploration of the lunar surface. These rovers will need to travel longer distances at higher speeds, and the efficient control of their paths is essential for mission success. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is a path tracking method with foresight and robustness, capable of predicting vehicle movement and solving optimization problems to minimize cost functions. However, the complexity of lunar environments necessitates simplified models, such as kinematic models, to reduce computational cost. The study proposes a special MPC method that uses zeroth-order gradient optimization to directly solve the nonlinear model and generate precise control commands, significantly reducing computational burden and meeting the computational cost requirements of lunar rover control.

articleTitle: Depth-Aware Knowledge Distillation Strategy Between ViTs and CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Model compression is an effective method to improve inference speed and reduce storage usage of neural networks. Knowledge Distillation (KD) is one of the typical model compression methods that adopts teacher-student training architecture to obtain a compact student model. The KD method has proved useful in various homogeneous distillation tasks while distilling between heterogeneous architectures is still unexplored. By using attention-based feature aligners in shallow layers of models and auxiliary decoupled distillation branches in deep layers, we propose a simple but powerful KD framework called Universal Heterogeneous KD (AHKD), which significantly increases heterogeneous distillation performance between CNNs and ViTs. Our proposed AHKD can work on multiple heterogeneous teacher-student pairs and obtain a maximum gain of 2.2 Top-1 accuracy on the CIFAR-100 dataset.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Geosynchronous Satellite Motion on Vehicle-borne SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Vehicle-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has the advantages of flexible configuration, convenient deployment, and long endurance, making it an effective means for high-resolution imaging of space targets such as geosynchronous (GEO) satellites. Due to the long distance between the SAR platform and the GEO satellite, it requires extremely long synthetic aperture time to achieve high-resolution imaging. In this case, GEO satellite motion cannot be ignored, which causes defocusing in SAR imaging. To address this issue, this paper derived an accurate slant range model between the GEO satellite and the vehicle-borne SAR platform. Based on this, the impact of GEO satellite motion on SAR imaging and the impact boundary are analyzed. The accuracy of the slant range model and the impact boundary is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: A Digital Simulation Model for Multi-Core Processors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Compared to single core processor simulation models, multi-core processor simulation models face unique problems in multi-core simulation, such as multi-core time system design, master-slave function planning between cores, and secure exit. Therefore, this article proposes a digital simulation model for multi-core processors and provides specific solutions to the above problems.

articleTitle: A New MRACS Design Scheme for Higher-Order System Follows Lower-Order Model Taking State Variables from the Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Model Reference Adaptive Control System (MRACS) design scheme for higher-order systems based on Popov hyperstability theory. The proposed approach enables higher-order systems to track lower-order models by utilizing state variables extracted directly from the model. To address the challenge of unmeasurable plant states and mitigate noise interference, a virtual ascending method is employed. Additionally, an adjustable linear compensator is introduced to eliminate the need for the strictly positive real condition. Simulation results demonstrate that the controlled plant effectively follows the reference model's output, validating the robustness of the proposed design.

Author Keywords: taking state variables from the model

articleTitle: Research of Multi-Satellite Mission Planning Method Based on Multi-Chromosome Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: As the number of satellites increases, traditional satellite mission planning methods, which rely on ground station planning and onboard execution, are becoming inadequate to meet the increasingly complex mission requirements. This paper proposes a multi-chromosome genetic algorithm to solve the problem of multi-satellite coordinated Earth observation mission planning. By analyzing the constraints of satellite observation tasks and resources, an optimization model is constructed with the goal of maximizing task completion weights. A multi-chromosome encoding method is designed to improve the algorithm's convergence speed and solution quality. Simulation results show that, compared to traditional genetic algorithms, this approach offers faster convergence and better optimization performance.

articleTitle: An Optimized Speed Curve Generation Algorithm for Trains Based on CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the continuous development of train control and communication technologies, trains are also developing towards automatic control and autonomous control. The train speed curve generation is one of the key research contents. Currently, some promising optimization algorithms of the train speed curve failure to meet the punctuality requirements in practical applications. For reducing the time of generating speed curve and improving the punctuality of the speed curve generation algorithm, an optimized speed curve generation algorithm for trains on the basis of Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) is proposed in this paper. This algorithm can learn the speed curves produced by different optimization algorithms or the speed curves of trains driven by excellent drivers, on the premise of ensuring energy-saving, punctuality, and other performance indexes of the curve. Based on the existing speed curve optimization algorithms, taking the Rolling Optimization Algorithm of Train Speed Curve(ROATSC) as an example without loss of generality, this paper uses the speed curve produced by this algorithm to train the CNN model, and uses the freight train as an example for simulation. Simulation results are achieved with different train weights and lengths, the CNN model speed curve fits the ROATSC algorithm speed curve with an approximation accuracy index 98%, which is higher than that of the Multilayer Perceptron(MLP) and Long Short-Term Memory network(LSTM) models. After testing, the speed curve produced by this method can not only decrease the generating time of speed curve, but also maintain the ROATSC algorithm performance. As seen in simulation results, the presented algorithm provides an additional choice to apply some algorithms of train speed curve generating in Automatic Train Control (ATO) system with the real-time requirement.

articleTitle: Application of MBSE in the Control Design of Control Moment Gyros on Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the advantages of design process visualization and modelization, model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is efficient to solve the problem such as the changeability of design requirement, the difficulty of carrying out verification at early stage. Oriented at the design requirement of spacecraft attitude control mission, the MBSE method is applied in the single gimbal control moment gyros (SGCMGs) control system. Through the process of requirement analysis, schematic design, simulation and verification, we model the SGCMGs control system requirements, establish the control framework, and analyze the interface between the facilities. The application is conducive to the integration and continuation of the relative knowledge and experience on spacecraft attitude control system.

articleTitle: A Dual-satellite Passive Positioning Method Based on Positioning Error Weights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: To enhance the detection capability of satellite systems for airborne targets, this paper proposes a dual-satellite passive positioning method that incorporates the weights of direction-finding errors. The method considers that the direction-finding error of the satellite relative to the target is influenced by distance. Based on the passive di-rection-finding results of the dual-satellite system, the target's position is determined by the weighted positioning error of each satellite on the common perpendicular segment of the dual-satellite direction-finding line. The fea-sibility of the proposed method is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Spaceborne Solid State Recorder Designed for High-Speed Space Detection Missions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This study presents a novel architecture for a high-speed solid-state recorder (SSR) specifically engineered for rapid space detection missions. The core components of this architecture include a data multiplexing unit, an array of error-correcting codes (ECC) utilizing the RS(256,252) algorithm, DDR3 high-speed cache, and a flash memory control unit. Noteworthy innovations feature a nine-stage pipeline for ECC processing with the RS(256,252) algorithm and advanced storage techniques for the flash memory control unit, including interleaved storage, multi-plane operations, and caching techniques. Additionally, the design incorporates a more optimized clock domain configuration. The SSR is designed to boost data throughput and error correction capabilities while maintaining reliable operation in the extreme conditions of outer space. System performance was evaluated using the K7 FPGA model, with a focus on throughput efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Vehicle Heading Deviation and Lateral Position Deviation by Combining Deep Learning and Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The path tracking control technology for unmanned vehicles based on visual perception has become increasingly mature in structured road scenarios. However, in unstructured roads, due to the significant increase in uncertainties in external environments and vehicle motion states, relevant research is still far from mature. The main issues faced by pure image perception algorithms in unstructured road scenarios include: the variability of external environments, significant impact of roads on vehicle motion states, which greatly affects image quality, leading to inaccurate vehicle state estimation and even abnormal jumps in the estimated values, severely affecting path tracking accuracy and driving safety. To address these issues, this paper designs a Kalman filter post-processing algorithm based on pure image perception algorithms using deep learning. This algorithm integrates the heading angle deviation and lateral position deviation estimated from images with the current actual vehicle speed. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method can effectively reduce estimation errors and suppress abnormal jumps in the estimated values. The algorithm was applied to real vehicle control on a grassland dirt road, and within a speed range of 0 to 20 km/h, the system operated stably, with normal road tracking, maintaining lateral position deviation within 0.6 meters and heading angle deviation within 0.05 radians.

articleTitle: Lidar-Basd Estimation of Rotation State for Small Body Rendezvous
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of flash-Lidar for rotation motion estimation in deep space applications, particularly its capability to navigate and perform maneuvers around small-body asteroids. Building upon a model registration algorithm, we first employ a weighted and scaled Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm to align the Lidar point cloud data with the target terrain model, enabling the calculation of the target's relative pose. Subsequently, we utilize rigid body dynamics theory to determine the absolute angular velocity and axis of rotation of the target. Through simulations, we assess the impact of varying angular velocity magnitudes and Lidar noise levels on the estimation of the target's rotational state. The findings indicate that the proposed approach effectively enhances motion estimation accuracy, paving the way for improved navigation in challenging deep space environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Key Observational Geometric Parameters for a Moon-Based Earth Observation Multispectral Imager
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Utilizing the Moon, the natural satellite, as an Earth observation platform and deploying a multispectral imager facilitates comprehensive observations of the Earth's large-scale phenomenon. In contrast to traditional space-borne platforms, a Moon-based multispectral imager observes the Earth from a long distance, and is directed towards the Earth using a turntable. In addition, the complex Sun-Earth-Moon geometry can also lead to issues with solar intrusion. All these factors pose challenges in the design of observational parameters. In this study, key observational geometric parameters are analyzed. The results indicated that the design of the Field of View (FOV) needs to take into account the maximum apparent radius of the Earth, the modification time interval, and pointing error. To ensure full observation of the Earth under any circumstances, the FOV diameter should be set to no less than 2.4°. During each synodic month, if the smallest angle between the sensor's line of sight and the solar direction falls below 5°, the Moon-based multispectral imager should pause its observations to evade the risk of solar intrusion. The temporal sampling interval is no longer greater than 4 h, and the spatial resolution is recommended not to exceed 20 km at the nadir point. All these findings obtained provide important basis for the design of parameters for the Moon-based multispectral imager.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Construction of Digital Lunar Base Based on 3D GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In the context of the development of manned lunar landing, lunar surface geographic information is the basis for lunar rover and astronauts to walk on the lunar surface, and its path navigation directly affects the personal safety of astronauts and the utilization of lunar surface resources. This paper aims at constructing a digital map of the lunar surface, combining the existing information of the lunar surface and geographic information system (GIS), and studies how to use the existing information base of the lunar surface map. A real-time digital map of lunar surface geographic resources, which integrates geographic resource query, map visualization, spatial statistical analysis, astronaut decision support and data sharing services, is further formed by using vehicle-mounted three-dimensional laser modeling to provide geographic resource information services with spatial analysis characteristics for future manned lunar surface autonomous navigation software.

articleTitle: Research on MTPA of PMSM Based on Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Maximum torque-current ratio control (MTPA) is a motor control strategy designed to optimize motor performance. Under this control strategy and based on vector control theory, this paper analyzed the nonlinear characteristics of permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) by decoupling method, the formulas of ID and IQ are derived. In the mean time, discusses the adjustment scheme of speed and current in detail, and summarizes the torque feature between maximum torque current ratio control and direct axis current id=0. Through Matlab/Simulimk simulation, comparing the control scheme of maximum torque current ratio and id = 0, the feasibility and superiority of fitting maximum torque current ratio curve control method are verified.

articleTitle: Dynamics and Nonlinearity of Combined Elastic Rimless Wheels with Bionic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The dynamics and nonlinearity of combined elastic rimless wheels(CERW) walking semi-passively along an inclined plane with bionic control is studied in this work. First, the dynamic model of CERW is established using the Lagrange method. Drawing inspiration from the visceral vibrations of animals during running, a bionic control system is designed to achieve cyclic walking in CERW. Finally, based on the derived dynamic model and bionic control system, simulation experiments are conducted to analyze the typical gaits and nonlinear phenomena of CERW under bionic control. The study focuses on nonlinear behaviors in the relationship between the oscillation frequency of telescopic masses and CERW walking frequency with bionic control, including phenomena like synchronization and bifurcation.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation System of Human-Computer Interaction Interface for Spacecraft Complex Information System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The human-computer interaction interface serves as the means for astronauts to control complex information systems, and with the advancement of manned deep space exploration, higher demands are placed on its design and evaluation. Establishing a comprehensive evaluation system can facilitate progress in human-computer interaction interface design. By analyzing the characteristics of spacecraft complex information systems' human-computer interaction interfaces and user traits, this study proposes evaluation index elements from three dimensions: task compliance, visibility, and usability. Index weights are determined through analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and expert scoring methods to construct an evaluation system for spacecraft complex information system's human-computer interaction interface.

articleTitle: A Complex Skill Learning Method Integrating Particle Swarm and Variational Autoencoder for Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Aiming to address the complex operation problems of robots in daily environments, this paper studies unstructured demonstration-learning method, enabling robots to complete complex tasks simply and naturally. Firstly, the demonstrator continuously demonstrates the complete process of executing complex tasks to obtain the robot's operation trajectory, and then BP-AR-HMM algorithm is used to automatically segment the complex trajectory into a sequence of single skills. Then, a variational autoencoder (VAE) and the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm are combined to learn the unlabeled demonstration skill sequence to reproduce the robot's complex operation trajectory. The PSO algorithm is explored to optimize the hyperparameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\beta}$</tex> in VAE model for improving learning accuracy and efficiency. The proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{PSO} -\boldsymbol{\beta}-\mathbf{VAE}$</tex> algorithm can enable the robot to learn complex operation skills under optimal conditions. To verify the effectiveness of our method, three demonstration scenarios were designed. The results show that the proposed method has high learning accuracy and short learning time in learning the skill sequences.

articleTitle: Multiple-Relational Attention for Vehicle Routing Problem with Simultaneous Delivery-Pickup
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The simultaneous delivery-pickup vehicle routing problem(VRPSDPTW) is a NP-hard problem, which has a wide application in modern logistics and distribution. A mathematical model is established to minimize the total vehicle cost, the total time cost and the customer dissatisfaction cost, then a multiple-relational attention RL(MARL) algorithm is proposed, involving the improved transformer-based model that provides dynamic-aware context embedding through an attention aggregation module on multiple relational structures. Experimental results conducted on standardized instances show that the MARL algorithm is able to couduct high-quality solutions in short computational time and outperforms the heuristic and learning-based algorithm comparisons.

articleTitle: Stable Inversion of Unstable Zeros for Iterative Learning Control and Application to CNC Machine Tool Precision Tracking Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Iterative Learning Control (ILC) is an excellent feedforward control method that can effectively suppress repetitive disturbances based on past error information. For motion platforms with good linearity, such as CNC machine tools, ILC design using inverse models remains the most effective. However, the presence of unstable zeros transforms the inverse model into an unstable pole, resulting in unbounded outputs. In discrete systems, unstable zeros primarily arise from: (1) non-collocated placement of actuators and sensors; (2) discretization using zero-order hold. Unstable zeros are common in motion control systems; therefore, this paper addresses these zeros using a time-domain noncausal stable inversion method to avoid phase and magnitude errors associated with conventional frequency-domain methods. Experiments conducted on a CNC machine tool motion stage with unstable zeros in X-axis demonstrate that the proposed method is effective for achieving precise motion control in CNC machine tools.

articleTitle: Lunar Exploration Robot Mobility and Stability: A Comprehensive Analysis and Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper conducts an in-depth study on the mobility and stability of lunar exploration robots in the complex lunar environment. By defining the robot's primary geometric parameters and two typical motion configurations, the paper analyzes the distribution of wheel loads, mobility performance, and stability performance. Specifically, considering the characteristics of the soft lunar soil, a contact dynamics model between the wheels and the soft lunar soil is established. The discrete element method (DEM) was used to simulate the lunar soil surface, and multi-body dynamics and DEM coupled simulation experiments were conducted. The experimental results indicate that the robot's mobility and stability are significantly affected by the height of the center of mass and ground clearance. The analysis of traction torque, sinkage, and slip ratio further verifies the accuracy and practicality of the model. This research provides theoretical foundations and technical support for the design and operation of lunar exploration robots.

articleTitle: Enhancing Hydrogen Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle Performance With Strategies Based on Optimized Equivalent Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The development of energy management strategies (EMS) is crucial for maximizing the performance and fuel economy of hydrogen fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle (HFCHEV). To enhance the robustness and adaptability of current energy management strategies for HFCHEV across various driving scenarios, this paper improves one of the most promising HFCHEV control schemes-the equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS). Based on the operating conditions of the hybrid power system (HPS) in dynamic driving environments, the design of the equivalent factor (EF) is optimized. Subsequently, an adaptive coefficient suitable for the current driving mode is integrated to establish a dynamic cost function that allows real-time adjustments. Finally, to evaluate the control effectiveness of the optimized strategy, a comparative simulation experiment with the dynamic programming (DP) strategy was conducted. The simulation results indicate that the optimized ECMS possesses performance nearly comparable to that of the DP strategy.

Author Keywords: Hydrogen fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle

articleTitle: Autofocus Method of Lunar Surface in-Situ Scanning Electron Microscope Based on Gaussian Defocus Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Lunar resources and environment exploration payload is the focus of space projects of various space powers. The miniaturized Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), which is widely used to analyze the morphology, composition and structure information of microscopic materials and substances, is a suitable payload for the exploration of lunar soil and rock structure and composition. Compared with the large bench scanning electron microscope in the laboratory, the micro electron microscope used for the in- situ exploration of the lunar surface puts forward higher requirements for the power consumption, efficiency and response speed of the control algorithm. The adaptive autofocus algorithm of electron beam is the core algorithm to drive the load. In this paper, an autofocus method based on Gaussian defocus model is proposed. The images collected by Zeiss scanning electron microscope and MATLAB simulation show that compared with the traditional method based on search algorithm, the proposed method significantly reduces the number of sampling frames and improves the focus speed.

articleTitle: Key Technology Research of Satellite-Ground Intergrated Design on Optical Remote Sensing Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the advancement of satellite technology, satellite manufacturing has evolved from being merely functional to being efficient and user-friendly. Designing satellites from the perspective of satellite-ground integration is a sophisticated approach to achieve efficiency and usability. This article summarizes several key technologies that require integrated satellite-ground design, based on the development experience of multiple optical remote sensing satellites. Foremost, the core indicator of satellite-ground integrated design is the accuracy of uncontrolled positioning. By analyzing the error chain, it is necessary to strictly control the orbit measurement error, star sensor attitude determination error, time synchronization error, and camera optical axis determination error throughout the satellite manufacturing process to ensure that the final uncontrolled positioning accuracy meets the requirements. Additionally, this article proposes suggestions for improving uncontrolled positioning accuracy both on the satellite and on the ground. The second key aspect involves designing the on-orbit radiometric calibration mode based on satellite-ground integration. To improve the frequency and quality of radiometric calibration, the satellite should be designed with imaging modes such as 90-degree yaw calibration and moon-oriented calibration, and the ground should be equipped with corresponding processing algorithms to achieve efficient on-orbit radiometric calibration and improve image quality. The third aspect involves designing the on-orbit geometric calibration mode, including star-oriented calibration and 180-degree yaw calibration, to enhance the frequency and effectiveness of geometric calibration. The fourth aspect focuses on designing the data transmission link for satellites carrying multiple payloads, ensuring that data is transmitted effectively through dual channels. Often, space-ground transmission errors can cause the loss of frames on a certain channel. If the data of multiple payloads are randomly distributed across dual channels, the loss of frames on one channel could result in the inability to merge data from the two channels, leading to payload data loss. Therefore, in the data transmission design, arranging the data of the same payload within the same channel is recommended to avoid the distribution of the same payload's data across two channels. This approach enhances the robustness of the entire system by ensuring that any data loss on a specific channel only affects one payload, without impacting the data of other payloads. Finally, the design of auxiliary data for payloads is addressed. The auxiliary data must be complete and accurate, including the platform's GNSS positioning and orbit determination information, the attitude information from star sensors, the angular velocity information from the gyroscope, the imaging time for each row, and the parameters used during imaging.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Inter-Cluster Communication Mechanism for Heterogeneous Multi-Cluster Intelligent System SoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With advancements in chip manufacturing technology and the increasing demand for workforce in intelligent systems, heterogeneous cluster architecture has emerged as a mainstream approach in System on Chip (SoC) design. Each SoC cluster is tailored to perform specific tasks, making inter-cluster communication essential for achieving the overall objectives of the SoC; its efficiency directly impacts performance metrics. In this article, we present a communication mechanism that integrates message passing and shared memory between clusters. This mechanism encompasses both hardware and software components, accommodates variable message lengths, and ensures low latency. Verification conducted on Palladium and HAPS simulation platforms demonstrates that with 256-byte messages under FreeRTOS conditions, the average delay is 4900 clock cycles between ARM clusters, approximately 4700 clock cycles between ARM and RISC-V clusters, and around 4600 clock cycles within RISC-V clusters. Compared to existing open-source communication mechanisms for heterogeneous clusters, our proposed solution significantly reduces inter-cluster delay.

articleTitle: Progress in Venus Exploration and Key Technology Research
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: At present, most of humanity's scientific understanding of Venus comes from early Venus's exploration results [1] [2]. In the past 20 years, Venus exploration has been at a low tide and no further exploration missions have been carried out deep into Venus's atmosphere. The early Venus and Mars exploration missions in the United States, the Soviet Union, and Europe were almost simultaneously carried out. There had many commonalities of the technology and products between the Venus probes and Mars probes. This article conducts research on the current research status of Venus exploration, and proposed key technologies such as system design technology of Venus probe, entering into aerodynamic configuration design and heat resistant structural technology, floating system design, thermal control technology under strong external heat flux environment, which can provide reference for future Venus exploration research in China.

articleTitle: Research on Motion Control of Wheel-Legged Robot Based on ASMC and LQR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Wheel-legged robots combine the high-speed movement of wheeled robots with the superior obstacle-navigation abilities of legged robots. To enhance the robot's resilience against disturbances and improve its ability to overcome obstacles, we developed a control scheme that decouples the control into two parts: posture control and balance control. First, the robot's dynamics were modeled using the Euler-Lagrange method. To manage external disturbances, an Adaptive Sliding Mode Controller (ASMC) was designed to handle posture control. For balance control, a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) was implemented to solve the Riccati equation in real-time, generating the necessary control torques to stabilize the robot. By combining these two control strategies, we present a framework that significantly improves the robot's mobility. Furthermore, tests conducted on a physical prototype demonstrated the effectiveness of the algorithm and the robot's disturbance rejection capability. The results confirm that the control scheme, which integrates ASMC and LQR, allows the wheel-legged robot to execute complex maneuvers and traverse uneven terrain with ease.

articleTitle: Feedback-Based Fusion Filtering for Rectangular Descriptor Systems via Amplify-and-Forward Relay Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the feedback-based fusion filtering problem for linear rectangular descriptor systems. By utilizing full-order transformation, the original descriptor system is transformed into a full-order non-descriptor system. Based on the measurement output forwarded by the relay and the feedback information from the fusion center, the local filters are constructed, and the upper bound of each filtering error covariance matrix is obtained by using the basic inequality and mathematical induction. Moreover, the local filter gain is derived by calculating the minimum value of the obtained upper bound. The local information is comprehensively processed by using the covariance intersection fusion criterion and the corresponding feedback-based fusion filtering algorithm is proposed. Finally, a numerical simulation is given to verify the effectiveness of the designed filtering algorithm.

articleTitle: A Coupled Dynamic Allocation Queue Management Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: For the multi-type business frame classification output model in broadband satellite adaptive transmission system, a coupled dynamic distributed queue management mechanism is proposed. Based on dynamic linked list storage allocation, this mechanism eliminates the risk of chain breakage and ensures the reliable operation of queue management module in satellite environment by improving the releasing strategy of occupied storage resources. The mechanism is suitable for multi-type task scenarios and has the characteristics of high storage utilization.

articleTitle: An Autonomous Reconfiguration Method for Satellite Constellation Network Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The satellite constellation is vast in scale with numerous nodes. Traditional software reconfiguration for satellite constellations requires individual reconfiguration for each node, leading to redundant software versions, heavy workloads, and low utilization of satellite visible segment. This paper addresses these issues by decoupling satellite parameters from software functions through satellite hardware and software settings, achieving satellite constellation uniformity of software versions. Furthermore, based on the satellite constellation network system, a “one-time upload, full-network reconfiguration” method is proposed, effectively tackling the challenges of software reconfiguration faced in traditional, especially giant satellite constellation. This approach allows for real-time reconfiguration of nodes outside satellite visible segment, significantly conserving valuable resources, reducing the workload for constellation reconfiguration, and enhancing efficiency. To ensure the safety and reliability of the reconfiguration process, the design of the autonomous rollback strategies ensures that satellites can continue to work normally even in a reconfiguration failure, thereby increasing the reliability of on-orbit reconfiguration.

articleTitle: A New MRACS Design Scheme for High-Order System Following Low-Order Model by Using State Variables Taking from the Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Based on Popov hyperstability, a new Model Reference Adaptive Control System (MRACS) design scheme for high-order system following low-order model using state variables taking from the model is proposed in this paper. Filters are used to reduce the order and the state variables are taken from the reference model. This scheme solves the problem of states of the plant can't be measured and improves anti-interference ability of the system. An adjustable linear compensator is introduced to remove the assumption of strictly positive real in Popov hyperstability theory. The simulation results show that the controlled plant can follow the output of the reference model well.

Author Keywords: Taking states variables from the model

articleTitle: A Framework of Distributed Hydraulic Support Control System Based on Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: As a vital energy source, coal mines are essential to the energy industry. However, the process of fully mechanized coal mining is notoriously harsh, which poses significant challenges to efficient and safe operations. In this context, hydraulic support operators play a crucial role in ensuring the stability and safety of the working face, where potential safety issues from operator errors or external interferences necessitate the adoption of smart mining practices. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a framework for a distributed hydraulic support control system based on a multi-agent system (MAS). First, by constructing this distributed multi-agent system within fully mechanized mining, the interactive relationship among hydraulic supports has been systematically delineated. Second, game theory is employed to inform decision-making regarding hydraulic support behaviors, enhancing both the autonomy and cooperation of the supports. Finally, the proposed model is analyzed and validated by maximizing the utility function, aiming to improve the efficiency and intelligence of fully mechanized mining operations. This comprehensive approach aims to ensure safer and more efficient coal mining practices through advanced technology integration and strategic decision-making.

articleTitle: Observability Analysis of Initial Relative Orbit Determination of Space Targets with Optical Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Autonomous spacecraft relative navigation has a wide range of applications in the field of on-orbit services. By virtue of its advantages of simplicity, reliability, small size, light weight and long acting distance, the optical camera has become the main measurement device for spacecraft relative navigation. However, since the optical camera can only acquire the line-of-sight information of the target and lacks the distance information, this limits the accuracy of spacecraft relative state estimation. Meanwhile, accurate initial relative orbiting is the foundation and key prerequisite for optical relative navigation. In order to improve the estimation accuracy and convergence speed of optical relative navigation, this paper proposes a method for analysing the observability of the initial relative state based on optical relative navigation. The observability of the initial relative state is analysed, and the method does not involve the operation of the Lie derivative, which significantly reduces the computational complexity of the observability analysis. Finally, the effects of orbital inclination, eccentricity and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_{2}$</tex> ingestion on LEO are simulated and analysed.

articleTitle: Multi-Revolution Optimal Rendezvous with Pertubation Near Elliptical Reference Orbit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: For multi-revolution rendezvous near elliptical reference orbit, the singularities of the semi-revolution and complete-revolution rendezvous are eliminated. The semi-revolution and complete-revolution rendezvous schemes are proposed, and an implementable rough-refinement two-step optimization algorithm is proposed to determine the optimal transfer time and two impulses. Based on the optimization process, a differential gradient iteration algorithm is presented to improve the rendezvous accuracy with the orbit perturbation considered. The multi-revolution two-impulse rendezvous optimization algorithm and iteration guidance algorithm can be easily extended to multiple-impulse rendezvous. Simulation examples of rendezvous near elliptical reference orbits with different eccentricities are performed. The results show that the optimization algorithm is accurate and effective, and the iteration algorithm converges rapidly. It is concluded that the optimization algorithm and the iteration guidance algorithm are suitable for perturbed multi-revolution rendezvous near circle reference orbit and arbitrary elliptical reference orbit. Several iterations can make the terminal rendezvous error less than one meter.

articleTitle: Close-Range Reconnaissance Control Method of Micro-Satellite with Hybrid Thrust Maneuver Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this paper, considering the thrust control problem of small satellites in GEO for close-Range reconnaissance, a control strategy based on hybrid thrust which integrates large impulse thrust with small continuous thrust is proposed. For pulse thruster, a multi-pulse thrust closed-loop control model based on the idea of switching control is constructed with maximum thrust constraint. Additionally, a genetic algorithm is introduced to realize the autonomous setting of the optimal parameter combination. Aiming at the the transition from the fly-around state to the hovering state, the fuel-optimized control method with limited fuel constraints is deduced based on a complex relative dynamics model incorporating continuous thrust integration. Then, according to the satellite hovering state characteristics, the finite thrust control model for hovering hold is derived to realize high-precision hovering observation. Finally, the simulation results of the 3D virtual platform and figures prove the feasibility and effectiveness of the hybrid thrust maneuver strategy for small satellites.

articleTitle: A Novel Collaborative Heterogeneous Supervision Network for Small Object Detection Method Based on Panchromatic and Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the increasing availability of simultaneous panchromatic and hyperspectral images, object detection methods based on them have demonstrated significant application advantages. However, they still face several challenges that limit detection performance: 1) the sizes of small objects remain very small even in the fused images, insufficient texture information and spectral information that is easily confused, leading to lower accuracy in object detection; 2) etection-by-Preprocess (DBP) methods often suffer from spectral and spatial detail distortions, compromising target features; 3) Preprocess-free detection (PFD) methods extract panchromatic and hyperspectral features directly through networks, but the black-box nature of deep network makes it difficult to ensure precise alignment of these two types of features, thereby hindering further improvements in detection accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposed a novel Collaborative Heterogeneous Supervision Network (CHS-Net) for small object detection on panchromatic and hyperspectral images. First, integrating fusion and detection components into a heterogeneous supervision network enhances learning capabilities by incorporating more empirical knowledge. Second, a unified joint regulation strategy was introduced to enhance integrated learning capabilities using optimized feedback loss functions. This approach enhanced the attention of different components to target features, effectively improving weak small target detection performance. Finally, comparative experiments based on EO-1 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms many start-of-the-art approaches.
