articleTitle: Controllability Analysis of Singular Heterogeneous Networked Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper investigates the controllability issue of networked dynamic systems with heterogeneous singular sub-systems. First, it analyzes the necessary conditions affecting system controllability. The results indicate that the observability of singular subsystems and the controllability of the system <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{i},\ A_{i},\ H_{i})$</tex> are necessary conditions for the controllability of networked systems; however, a networked system may still be controllable even if the network topology or subsystems are uncontrollable. Then, the paper provides the necessary and sufficient conditions for controllability under general network topologies. It reveals the impact of factors such as network topology structure, external inputs, subsystem dynamics, and state couplings between subsystems on the controllability of singular heterogeneous networked systems. Additionally, it examines the necessary and sufficient conditions for controllability when the network topology matrix is diagonalizable. Finally, several examples are provided to illustrate the results of the study.

articleTitle: A SLAM Method for Indoor Degradation Environment Based on Lidar/IMU/UWB Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Currently, 3D Lidar is widely used in indoor SLAM tasks due to its stable and reliable measurement performance. However, it suffers from significant positioning and mapping errors in indoor degraded environments, making it difficult to ensure high global consistency. This issue has long constrained its development. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an indoor mobile robot SLAM algorithm based on multi-sensor information fusion. This method bypasses the need for relying solely on degraded state estimation, thereby overcoming the limitations of a single sensor in real-world environments by leveraging complementary features between sensors to solve the indoor degradation problem. This paper integrates Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), Ultra-Wideband (UWB) ranging, and Lidar information, and designs a complete SLAM algorithm framework based on nonlinear optimization and an error-state Kalman filter. At the same time, the degradation level of the point cloud perceived by the Lidar is used as a key basis for selecting the UWB residual weight, thereby addressing the problem of indoor Lidar point cloud degradation. Finally, this paper demonstrates the superiority of the algorithm through real-world experiments.

articleTitle: Obstacle Detection Based on the Fusion of Telephoto and Wide-Angle Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: With the rapid development of contemporary society, rail transit plays an increasingly important role in our daily lives, and higher requirements are put forward for safety and intelligence. The current object detection methods only use a single telephoto or short-focus camera for image acquisition, which cannot meet the requirements of long-distance and wide-angle detection. In response to the specific needs of object detection in rail transit application scenarios, this paper proposes a Simulated Annealing-based Normalized Cross-correlation Matching Algorithm to fuse the images of telephoto and short-focus cameras to improve the range and distance of obstacle detection. In view of the fact that most current object detection models adopt a single-input-single-output structure, in order to effectively combine the fused images and the short-focus images that provide supplementary information, this paper proposes a Dual-Input Fusion Transformer YOLO (DIFT-YOLO) network model. Finally, in order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model, it was rigorously tested using the image data set collected on-site. The results show that under the same object detection network model, the image detection accuracy after the SA-NCC matching and fusion is 1.9% higher than that of the original short-focus image and 1.8% higher than that of the image after NCC matching. Compared with the single-input merged image model, the DIFT-YOLO model improves the mAP by 7.3%.

articleTitle: Digital Twin System for Smart Campuses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In an era where educational institutions are increasingly embracing technology to improve efficiency and enhance learning environments, the concept of smart campuses has emerged as a crucial development. The traditional approach of monitoring campus environments through video footage and manual inspections is becoming outdated as technology advances. To empower smarter campus management and enhance the educational experience, this study presents a systematic approach for smart campuses built on the foundation of digital twins. This technology creates a virtual replica of the physical campus, enabling real-time monitoring of various aspects like security, teaching, maintenance, environment, assets, and energy usage. We simulate real-world campus behavior by constructing this digital counterpart. The resulting digital twin image can be visualized through various user-friendly interfaces, including virtual reality and 3D models, empowering managers to make informed decisions for a more efficient and secure campus environment. Implementing a digital twin system in a smart campus setting demonstrates significant improvements in operational efficiency, security management, and environmental sustainability. By leveraging the power of digital twins, educational institutions can transition towards smarter, more responsive, and sustainable campus environments, ultimately enriching the educational experience for students and staff.

articleTitle: An Improved Fault-Tolerant Control and Stabilization for Positive Polynomial Fuzzy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper presents an improved analysis method to design a fault-tolerant controller for positive polynomial fuzzy systems based on static output feedback as well as actuator faults. Firstly, inspired by the property of fault matrix, a new approach of controller design is presented, and some constraint conditions are introduced to guarantee the stability conditions and posi-tivity conditions to be convex simultaneously. Furthermore, by comparing with the existing methods, this method not only can eliminate the binding to the input matrix B, but also is able to provide a wider range of stability region. Besides, to enhance the relaxation of the stability analysis, we introduce the up-to-date Taylor series membership functions (TSMFs) approximation method such that the information embedded in the membership functions and the state boundary information can be taken into the stability conditions. As a result, on the strength of Lyapunov stability theory, the stability analysis is performed via sum-of-squares (SOS) approach. Finally, a simulation example is given to illustrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Embodied Intelligence Technology in Space Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Embodied intelligence technology belongs to artificial intelligence (AI) technology, which is one of the embodiments. Compared to traditional operation robots, the greatest advancement of intelligent operation robots is their intelligence based on the large models, enabling cognitive understanding of the world and intelligent decision-making. Specifically, from the perspective of application, the essence of embodied intelligence is the agent's ability to autonomously perceive, make decisions, and execute actions from the first perspective. Embodied intelligence emphasizes the close connection between the agent and the environment. The agent perceives and understands the environment autonomously through the first perspective. It makes autonomous decisions, interacts with and adapts to the environment through autonomous execution. This article conducts exploratory research on the practical application of embodied intelligence technology in space missions from two aspects: on-orbit service and planetary exploration. This research can provide reference for the practical space application of artificial intelligence technology.

articleTitle: Damage Prediction of Underground Engineering by Adaptive Network Based Fuzzy Inference System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Extensive research on the penetration damage caused by warheads has revealed limitations in studies that focus solely on a single geological material or concrete medium, as well as those that only evaluate penetration depth. Such approaches fail to adequately capture the damage inflicted by explosions and shock waves on underground tunnel engineering. To address these shortcomings and fulfill the need for accurate damage prediction in scenarios where underground engineering is impacted by warheads, this paper proposes a novel prediction approach based on an adaptive fuzzy neural network system. This system integrates penetration damage and shock wave overpressure damage to predict the overall level of damage to underground structures caused by various warheads, including ground-penetrating bombs. By employing the target vulnerability and warhead power stratification method, this research evaluates the degree of damage inflicted. The adaptive fuzzy neural network is utilized to predict potential damage to crucial elements within tunnel engineering, such as protective systems.

articleTitle: Autonomous Multi-Task Reliability Allocation Method for Unmanned Swarms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The technology of autonomous unmanned swarm systems, as a disruptive innovation poised to transform future technological development, is gaining increasing attention. It has the capability to autonomously complete critical tasks such as mapping, search and rescue, and strikes in harsh, dangerous, or otherwise inaccessible environments. This technology is playing an increasingly significant role across various fields, including national defense, meteorology, and exploration. Consequently, the demands for its reliability in executing complex tasks are also rising. However, due to the autonomy of individual units within the swarm and the coordination required among them, it is challenging to effectively allocate reliability metrics to individual unmanned units. Traditional reliability allocation methods, which consider factors like complexity and environmental conditions, are not well-suited for these systems. This paper, drawing on the multi-task behavioral patterns of autonomous unmanned swarms and considering the fault-recovery characteristics during mission execution, proposes a reliability allocation method based on dynamic trade-off strategies. This method aims to provide a reference for the allocation of reliability metrics in autonomous unmanned swarms.

articleTitle: Smooth Soft Actor-Critic for Free-Floating Cable-Driven Robot Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The Free-floating Cable-Driven Robot (FCDR) is an advanced multi-joint rigid robot driven by cable tension, offering high flexibility, low cost, lightweight structure and the ability to carry large loads, making it ideal for space tasks. However, controlling FCDR is challenging due to complex cable dynamics and material properties. Traditional control methods like optimal and fuzzy control require manual adjustments, while adaptive controllers, though robust, are complex and unstable. Recently, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown promise in FCDR control due to its excellent generalization and adaptability. Techniques such as Deep Q-Network (DQN), Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) have been applied to improve FCDR performance, with SAC standing out for its accuracy and error handling in continuous control tasks. Our approach smooth Soft Actor-Critic (SSAC) combines SAC, target policy smoothing and cost function estimation to enhance trajectory planning stability. Simultaneously, our comparative experiments between Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) and SAC demonstrate that shaped dense reward functions are more effective than sparse reward functions. This work highlights the advancements in DRL for FCDR control, addressing both static and dynamic operational challenges.

articleTitle: An AD-SPSO Algorithm for Solving the Measurement Resource Scheduling Problem with Satellite Cataloging Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Under the condition of limited ground measurement resources, the increasing scale of satellites brings more satellite cataloging requirements and aggravates the measured pressure. How to better utilize limited measurement resources is a crucial issue. In this paper, the measurement resource scheduling problem with satellite cataloging requirements is examined, a measurement resource scheduling model is established with the goal of maximizing profits from satellite cataloging task completion, and a switching particle swarm optimization algorithm based on adaptive large neighborhood search and dynamic neighborhood (AD-SPSO) is proposed. The AD-SPSO algorithm uses the time greedy strategy and chaos mapping to obtain an initial population with better quality. Then, the algorithm designs the dynamic neighborhood of the particle, after which the particle's velocity is updated by selecting the optimal position from the dynamic neighborhood of the particle, so as to enhance the inter-particle information interaction and utilize the population information. In addition, the AD-SPSO algorithm joins the adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm, which selects different particles for perturbation according to the population state. This effectively prevents its early convergence. To evaluate the performance of the AD-SPSO algorithm, this paper performs experiments in four scenarios, and in different scenarios, compared with other improved algorithms, the AD-SPSO algorithm can obtain higher and more stable overall profit for scheduling plans, which verifies its effectiveness in solving the measurement resource scheduling problem with satellite cataloging requirements.

articleTitle: Research on High Precision Autonomous Navigation Method of Cruise Phase of Deep Space Exploration Based on Observation Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The cruise phase of deep space exploration is one of the important stages of the small body exploration mission, and the autonomous navigation accuracy of the cruise phase will also be of great significance to the successful implementation of the subsequent small body exploration mission. Because the probe needs to determine its own state independently in the detection process, the calculation burden is large, so it is difficult to effectively achieve high navigation accuracy and meet the detection requirements. In response to the above problems, this paper constructs the autonomous navigation system model of the cruise phase of the deep space probe, analyzes the observability conditions of the system combined with the observability theory, and gives the quantitative index of autonomous navigation accuracy, so as to select the optimal combination of observation targets to make the navigation accuracy maximum. Finally, the small body detection is used as the background for simulation verification, and the simulation results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this paper, we study the stability problem of second-order linear active disturbance rejection control of second-order linear systems without external disturbances. The state space model of the closed-loop system is established through two subsystems, state feedback and linear extended state observer error, and the convergence of the closed-loop system is analyzed with the help of the characteristic equations of the state space model. When the system internal disturbance is known, the stability condition for the closed-loop subsystem is obtained as long as the derivative of the system disturbance satisfies the Lipschitz condition. When the system internal disturbance is not considered and the system internal disturbance is unknown, two methods of Nyquist stability criterion and Lyapunov function are applied respectively, and the system is asymptotically stabilized over a large range by theoretical analysis and mathematical proof, and the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Position Probability Prediction Method of Marine Moving Targets for Optimization Search by Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Marine moving ship target search has great application demand and development prospects in marine surveillance, marine search and rescue, customs anti-smuggling, and other aspects. Satellites are a vital means of searching for marine moving targets. Ground coverage for imaging satellites is relatively limited; the vast marine area makes searching for marine moving ships challenging. Target position prediction, used as the guidance information for satellite detection to reduce the uncertainty of the target position and improve search efficiency, is an essential approach to achieving target optimization search. This paper proposes a target position prediction method based on joint learning of multi-source factors for optimal satellite search of marine moving targets. Firstly, it analyzes the characteristics of marine moving targets and the factors affecting motion. Then, it puts forward the motion prediction model based on a deep neural network, integrating multifactor, like the state of the moving target, environmental attributes such as nautical charts, meteorology and hydrology, and kinematic constraints, to predict the target positional distribution probability. Finally, the target search strategy based on the maximum sum of the distribution probabilities of the satellite coverage area is adopted to improve target detection probability. The experiment results show that the prediction method can realize the target positional distribution probability prediction, reduce the uncertainty search when making the satellite search plan, and improve efficiency.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pitch Angle Tracking Control For Noncanonical Nonlinear Aircraft Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This study addresses the challenging problem of pitch angle tracking control for noncanonical nonlinear aircraft systems. Traditional control schemes for pitch angle tracking are primarily designed based on the Lyapunov function for canonical systems. However, due to the lack of information regarding the relative degree of controlled system, the design methods of traditional control schemes are not suitable for the noncanonical systems. To overcome this difficulty, this paper constructs a parameterizable high-order recurrent neural network to approximate the noncanonical nonlinear aircraft system so that the designed difficulty caused by unknown relative degree can be resolved. Based on the approximation system, we further propose. and proposes a novel gradient-based adaptive tracking control scheme based on this approximation system. By employing an advanced gradient adaptive update law and integrating parameter projection technology, the scheme can ensure asymptotic tracking performance and boundedness of all closed-loop signals. The controller can actively avoid potential singularities and enhance the robustness of the controller against model uncertainties and external disturbances. The simulation results based on the twin otter aircraft effectively demonstrate the significant effectiveness and superiority of the control scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a 1553B Communication and Control Software System for Deep Space Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: As an important data communication method in the field of deep space exploration, the 1553B bus is commonly used in the construction of information network and data interaction between multiple instruments and segments of spacecraft. This artical focus on the 1553B data communication requirements of the spaceborne probe payload subsystem, introduces the 1553B bus communication method between a certain type of scientific exploration payload and the on-board payload controller for a deep space exploration mission in China. It details the configuration and control process of chips such as AT697F and B65170S6RH,as well as the software and hardware design architecture, including the comprehensive electronic processing module architecture and software task division, multitasking synchronization method, and 1553B bus data receiving and transmitting process. Regarding the harsh environment and SEU(Single Event Upset) effect in space, It also introduces the reliability method for aerospace software design. Finally, based on the 1553B bus data simulation software designed by the 1553B bus simulation device, the payload main control software has been tested for function and performance, and the test results were in line with the design indicators.

articleTitle: Random-Fuzzy Risk Tree Approach for Assessing Fire Hazard in Sub-healthy Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper delves into the application of risk sensitivity analysis using a random-fuzzy risk tree framework for evaluating the fire risk associated with recalled electric vehicles (EVs). The proposed methodology aims to prioritize the significance of fire hazards within the EV system. Specifically, it assesses the extent to which risk probabilities at the basic event level influence the overall system-level risk probability. Recalled EVs often represent sub-healthy vehicles that harbor potential risks, including the threat of fires, which are characterized by latency, randomness, and fuzziness. Furthermore, there exists no clear-cut correlation between fire risk and various influencing factors. To date, there has been a paucity of specialized theoretical research focusing on risk information from the unique perspective of fire hazards in sub-healthy EVs. The present study collects recall bulletins issued in China over a four-year period, identifies fire hazards in diseased, sub-healthy EVs, and constructs a fire risk tree that unravels the fundamental influencing factors and their logical causal relationships. Leveraging random-fuzzy theory, we evaluate the risk sensitivity, accurately determining the influence weights of various risk hazards and prioritizing potential weak links. This combined approach integrates random-fuzzy analysis with sensitivity assessment, providing valuable insights for addressing fire hazards in sub-healthy EVs.

articleTitle: Distributed Formation Control for Fixed-Wing UAVs with Input MRS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In this paper, the distributed formation tracking control problem is investigated for multiple fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) considering input magnitude and rate saturation (MRS) constraints. First, a first-order input MRS model is constructed. Next, the distributed leader state observer is designed to facilitate the acquisition of the leader information for each follower UAV. Then, by virtue of the backstepping method and the disturbance observer, the formation control law for each fixed-wing UAV is designed and the stability analysis is presented using the Lyapunov theory. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the performance of the designed control strategy.

articleTitle: Backstepping Control of Multi-input Extremum Seeking Systems Based on State Feasible Region Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: In order to solve the control problem of multi-input extremum seeking systems based on state feasible region constraint, extremum seeking method, backstepping control and adaptive control were combined. Firstly, system states' extremum reference trajectory was designed by extremum seeking method. Secondly, backstepping controller was designed by appropriate Lyapunov function selected by inversion control method. At last, unknown parameters estimation law were designed by adaptive control method. Objective function extreme value is seeked under the condition of feasible region constraint is satisfied. Simulation result shows that the proposed design method is effectiveness.

articleTitle: Switched Sliding Mode Control for Networked T-S Fuzzy Delayed Systems: A Membership Function-Dependent Event-Triggered Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: This paper investigates the switched sliding mode control (SMC) problem for networked T-S fuzzy delayed systems with limited communication capability, where the event-triggered mechanism is adopted to schedule the information transmission. Using the fuzzy model and controller membership function information, a membership function-dependent dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is constructed with hope to enhance effective data utilization. Furthermore, a novel switched fuzzy sliding mode controller is designed. Then, by combining with the membership function analysis method, sufficient conditions are provided to guarantee that the closed-loop fuzzy system is asymptotically stable with a prescribed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance and the sliding surface is reachable. Finally, a simulation example is employed to demonstrate the rationality of proposed switched SMC strategy.

articleTitle: AODS: Adaptive Obstacle Detection System for Smart Wheelchairs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: The rising global demand for smart mobility solutions underscores the critical need for advanced technologies in power wheelchairs to ensure the safety and independence of users with mobility challenges. This work introduces a novel segmentation-based pipeline for obstacle detection, specifically tailored for outdoor environments, to enhance navigational safety in smart wheelchairs. The segmentation model within the pipeline addresses prevalent issues in current technologies-such as variable lighting conditions, scale changes, and distance sensitivity-that significantly affect detection accuracy. The proposed model incorporates innovative components, including a Distance Augmentation Module (DAM), Scale Aware Module (SAM), and an Illumination Simulation Module (ISM), ensuring robust performance under diverse operational conditions. Validation on a specially curated dataset from urban settings in Chengdu, China, demonstrates a segmentation accuracy of 86.0%, out-performing existing solutions. The findings suggest substantial improvements in detecting and navigating around obstacles, thereby significantly enhancing the operational efficiency and safety of smart wheelchairs. This work not only contributes a sophisticated algorithmic approach and a tailored dataset to the field but also verifies the practical efficacy of the model through extensive experimental validation.

articleTitle: Pareto-Optimal Coverage Control for Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Systems: A General Sum Game Reinforcement Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Control Science and Systems Engineering (ICCSSE)
abstract: Individual performance variations, target conflicts, and dynamic scenarios pose challenges in creating effective solutions to balance individual and collective benefits in collaborative multi-agent area coverage control. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a semi-distributed Pareto-optimal policy iteration algorithm (SDPOPI). This algorithm introduces a multi-objective group game (MOGG) model that accounts for conflicting objectives such as coverage efficiency, group density, energy consumption, and communication topology equilibrium. By guiding the distributed reinforcement learning policy iteration process through a game interaction mechanism, the algorithm establishes a dual-layer semi-distributed policy iteration frame-work that achieves the Pareto-Nash equilibrium for the MOGG, thereby balancing individual and group benefits. Simulation results validate the accuracy and practical applicability of the proposed method.
